epic.title: Redesign the web UI in the ink-and-paper visual language
epic.description: Apply the Genie design system (docs/assets/brand/design-system.md, principles.md, components.html, handoff/) to every screen of the web UI. Redesign the board, task list, task detail, epics, team view and agent chat, authentication, the answer page and the shell; reskin documentation, the agents catalogue, other platform pages and Settings. Behaviour, routes, URLs, shortcuts and server contracts do not change.
ac: Every screen in handoff/screens.md is implemented in both themes (ink and paper) at desktop and phone widths
No hard-coded colours, font families or legacy design variables remain outside tokens.css
All existing routes, URL parameters, keyboard shortcuts, drag and drop and live updates behave as before
Accessibility audit passes and the token contrast test covers every colour token
The documentation site and README use the new brand
A PR is published and CI passes for its latest head
epic.plan: Phase 0 prepare (H00, H01); phase 1 foundation (H02-H07); phase 2 screens (H10-H19); phase 3 reskin (H20-H23); phase 4 close-out (H30-H33). See handoff/tasks.md for dependencies and parallel lanes.

tasks.title: Build the verification harness: seeded throwaway server and screenshot script
tasks.description: Agents cannot judge a redesign without seeing it. Build a repeatable way to run the web UI against realistic data and capture screenshots of every route in both themes. Start a throwaway Genie server (cargo run -p genie -- serve with a temporary data directory) and seed it through the genie CLI or the HTTP API with a project containing tasks in all eleven statuses, epics with children, tasks with acceptance criteria and PR/CI data, owner decisions, notifications, documents, and as many teams and mailboxes as can be created without live agents (record the gap if teams need fixtures). Capture screenshots with Playwright using the preinstalled Chromium (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, executablePath /opt/pw-browsers/chromium; do not run playwright install). Check whether npm ci passes on a clean checkout before adding any dependency; the lock file may be out of sync.
ac: One documented command seeds a throwaway server and prints its URL; it never touches the local tracker or real data
One command captures PNGs for every route listed in handoff/screens.md in ink and paper at 1440x900 and 390x844, with animations disabled and a fixed clock, into an ignored output folder
The set of baseline screenshots of the current UI is captured and attached to the task before any redesign begins
The seed covers all eleven statuses, epics, owner decisions, notifications and documents; known gaps (for example teams) are listed in docs/development.md
docs/development.md explains how to run the harness
tasks.plan: Investigate server startup and seeding via the ops catalog; write the seed script; write the Playwright capture script; capture baselines; document.

tasks.title: Split app/styles.css by area with no visual change
tasks.description: app/styles.css is one 1,144-line file shared by every screen, which would make parallel redesign work conflict. Split it by its own section markers (shell, list, board, detail, team, overlays, mobile, additions, epics, docs, filters, task preview) into per-area stylesheets next to the code that uses them (FSD layers), imported where used. Keep selectors, order-dependent cascade, and values identical.
ac: styles.css contains only the root variables, resets and genuinely global rules
Each area stylesheet is imported by the component that owns it
Screenshots before and after are pixel-identical for all routes and both viewports
npm run typecheck, npm run lint:web and npm run build:web pass
tasks.plan: Map every rule to an owner; move in small commits; diff screenshots after each move; fix cascade-order regressions.

tasks.title: Fonts, tokens, theme switch, and legacy compatibility layer
tasks.description: Make the design tokens live in the app. Self-host Unbounded and Manrope (variable, Latin and Cyrillic subsets, OFL) through the build instead of Google Fonts, so a self-hosted or offline Genie renders correctly. Import tokens.css and components.css. Add a theme switch: data-theme on the html element with values system, ink and paper, persisted as a preference, with a matching theme-color meta. Add a compatibility block that maps every legacy variable (--bg, --text, --muted, --accent, --amber, --line, ...) to the new tokens so existing CSS adopts the palette immediately. See design-system.md and tokens.css.
ac: No request to fonts.googleapis.com remains; fonts load from the bundle and work offline
The app renders in the new palette in both themes; no text is unreadable (verified with the harness screenshots)
A theme preference (system, ink, paper) persists and applies before first paint without a flash
Every legacy variable is aliased in one clearly marked compatibility block
test/design-tokens.test.ts passes; the legacy block is listed for removal in H33
tasks.plan: Add font packages; import styles; theme bootstrap script in index.html; write the alias block; verify with screenshots.

tasks.title: Character component and state hook
tasks.description: Bring the character into the app. Make the four animated SVGs from docs/assets/brand/character/ available to the bundle (import as assets), add a Genie component (state, size, alt) that respects reduced motion, and a pure function plus hook that derives the state from teams and tasks: thinking when any member is working, sleeping when nothing is active, waking transiently when a team becomes active, surprised when a task returns to changes requested, CI fails, or a decision arrives. Use it in the status dock and the shared EmptyState. If the live event stream lacks a needed signal, degrade to thinking and sleeping and document the gap; do not change server contracts in this task.
